name: NVIDIA B200
memory_bandwidth_basis: 8 TB/s as printed by NVIDIA. 186GB HBM3e over an 8,192-bit dual-reticle-die bus at 8 TB/s; the die count is 2 (two reticle-limited dies joined by a 10 TB/s chip-to-chip link, presented as one GPU).
notes: AUDIT CORRECTION: the dense/sparse flag on the tensor rows was inverted. FP16 2500 / FP8 5000 / FP4 10000 TFLOPS are DENSE; the datasheet prints 5/10/20 PFLOPS 'Specifications in sparse. Dense is one-half of the sparse spec shown.' These rows were previously flagged dense:false, which wrongly told a reader they were sparse.  The stored numbers are correct dense values. CRITICAL: NVIDIA's Blackwell datasheet states 'Specifications in sparse. Dense is one-half of the sparse spec shown.' The printed per-GPU figures are FP4 20 PFLOPS, FP8/FP6 10 PFLOPS, INT8 10 POPS, FP16/BF16 5 PFLOPS, TF32 2.5 PFLOPS, FP32 80 TFLOPS, FP64 40 TFLOPS - ALL SPARSE. Dense is half: 10 / 5 / 5 / 2.5 / 1.25 PFLOPS as recorded. A '10 PFLOPS FP8' claim for B200 is therefore a SPARSE number; dense FP8 is 5 PFLOPS. tdp_w 1000 is the HGX B200 'configurable up to 1,000W' figure - this is per-accelerator (per dual-die GPU), not per board. 'vram_gb' 186 is per accelerator across both dies. Source is a reseller-hosted copy of NVIDIA's PDF because NVIDIA's own resources.nvidia.com copy is a JS viewer; treat figures as vendor-claim only. The 'other' rows are FP64 and FP64 Tensor Core (both 40 TFLOPS, sparse / 20 dense as printed together on the sheet) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
